title: The Cat’s Paw and Lobster Nebulae
caption: The Cat's Paw and Lobster Nebulae, imaged by ESO's VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: Cat's Paw Nebula, Lobster Nebula · constellation Scorpius

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The Cat's Paw Nebula, NGC 6334, at upper right, and the Lobster Nebula, NGC 6357, at lower left, share this giant image from the VLT Survey Telescope. Their gas glows red, and dark clouds of dust weave through the very rich star field around them.

Both are regions of active star formation. Hot young stars inside them are pouring out energetic light that makes the surrounding hydrogen gas shine red, the characteristic glow of hydrogen that has been energized in this way.

The picture is huge, with around two billion pixels, making it one of the largest images ESO has released. That scale lets viewers zoom from the full sweep of both nebulae right down to small details within them. The circular features around bright stars are not real, though. They are reflections inside the optics of the telescope and camera.

understand.summary: This image was made with the OmegaCAM camera on ESO's VLT Survey Telescope, using g and r filters and a narrow-band filter. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
filters: 480 nm · Optical g (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
625 nm · Infrared r (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
852 nm · Optical z=0.3 H-Alpha, NB (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
understand.eye: The long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so the red glow and dark dust clouds appear much more vivid than they would to an observer.
